title: Backyard Putting Greens in Wellington, CO | NoCo Turf Co.
description: Wellington planned artificial-turf greens for Colorado's first MultiGolfPark. What Buffalo Creek's HOA rules and the Town's code mean for a backyard green.
h1: Colorado's first MultiGolfPark is in Wellington, with artificial turf planned for its 9 hole greens
lede: No golf course sits inside Wellington. The Town's planned turf greens are small and public: 9 MultiGolf holes in Knolls Linear Park, where the Town said in June 2026 that artificial turf would cover the concrete hole greens. A backyard green here answers to Buffalo Creek-style HOA guidelines more often than to the Town.

answer.question: Can I put a putting green in my Wellington backyard?
answer.answer: Most likely, but check two things. Wellington's landscape standards skip single-family building permits, yet its code wants a permit for an accessory use added after the house unless exempted, and a green isn't named; ask Wellington Planning. In Buffalo Creek, the 2019 guidelines still say artificial turf is prohibited; Colorado's backyard rule, printed here, applies. NoCo Turf Co. installs backyard putting greens in Wellington.

blocks.h2: The Town's own artificial-turf greens are on a 9-hole MultiGolf course.
blocks.takeaway: Wellington's MultiGolfPark, which the Town calls the first in Colorado, mixes disc golf, foot golf and park golf on one compact course.
paras: Crews from the Parks and Recreation and Public Works departments were installing it in Knolls Linear Park in June 2026, with direction from course designer Avery Jenkins. The 9 holes run 1,790 feet in all, from 135 to 235 feet each.

The Town said finishing the course later that summer would add artificial turf over the concrete bases of all 9 hole greens and tee pads. No Town page checked on September 25, 2026 says the turf is down, so treat it as the plan, not the finished course.

blocks.h2: Buffalo Creek's posted guidelines still say artificial turf is prohibited.
paras: Buffalo Creek at Wellington publishes Residential Improvement Guidelines last revised June 13, 2019. Its xeriscaping section, written for areas of a lot where sod is being replaced, says artificial turf or plants are prohibited, and a separate line keeps Astro-turf off walks, front steps and decks.

The drainage rule reaches a green even where the turf question is settled: any change affecting drainage needs Architectural Review Committee approval, and the committee may ask for a drainage engineer's report. The same guidelines want each yard to keep at least 2,000 square feet of irrigated sod, up to 2,900, or drought-tolerant vegetative landscape, and a turf green is neither.
The 2019 revision is older than the Colorado rule printed below. The Town's own front-yard rule, which a front green would meet first, is on the [Wellington page](/areas/wellington-co/).

blocks.h2: For a green in a new HOA park, Wellington's park standard is the open question.
blocks.takeaway: Wellington's code names chipping and putting greens as functional artificial turf, then steers turf in new parks to fields and play space.
paras: Section 15-9-20 counts the playing areas of golf courses, putting and chipping greens included, as functional artificial turf, and defines plain turf as living, regularly mowed nonnative grass.

Section 15-5-40 covers new public parks, pocket parks, detention ponds, trail connections and common open space for public or HOA use. It caps functional turf at 50% of a park's landscaped area and says only high-traffic areas such as sport fields and informal play space next to playgrounds shall contain functional or high-water turf.

Read together, those lines leave an artificial putting green in a new HOA amenity area unsettled: functional turf by definition, but neither a sport field nor play space. It depends on the site plan; ask Wellington Planning. Not legal advice.

faq.q: Does a backyard putting green need a Town permit in Wellington?
faq.a: It depends. Section 15-4-40 requires a building permit, unless exempted, for an accessory use or building proposed after the house, and leaves accessory uses it doesn't name to the Planning Director case by case. A putting green isn't named, and retaining walls must be designed for the lateral pressure of the ground they hold (Section 15-5-30). Ask Wellington Planning before you build.

faq.q: Can I put a net or a tall fence behind a chipping area?
faq.a: Wellington caps an opaque privacy fence at 6 feet on a rear property line or a side yard line in the rear yard, and lets a fence around a recreation court or a publicly owned recreation area go higher only if it is at least 50% open (Section 15-5-30). A backyard chipping net isn't named, so ask Wellington Planning before putting one up.

faq.q: My subdivision isn't Buffalo Creek. Where do I check?
faq.a: Your HOA's covenants and design guidelines first, then the Colorado rule on this page. Town review and HOA review are separate, so a green can clear one and still need the other.
